articles.title: US Measles Cases Jump by 426 in One Week to 5,838, the Largest Rise in Decades
articles.excerpt: The CDC's latest tally is the first since the Pan American Health Organization declared measles endemic in the United States again, ending an elimination status held since 2000.
articles.image_caption: A baby with measles in the Philippines, in a 2014 CDC Global photograph. Confirmed US measles cases rose by 426 in one week to 5,838 as of November 19, according to the CDC.
articles.nri_angle: With 5,838 confirmed cases across 47 jurisdictions and kindergarten MMR coverage down to 92.4%, US-based Indian families should verify every household member's MMR record, especially before holiday travel.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ICMR Survey Puts Anaemia at 56% of Women, Severe Cases Below 2%
articles.excerpt: SAMPADA, ICMR's venous-blood survey of more than 2 lakh people across 183 districts, finds most anaemia is mild and iron deficiency explains only about half of cases among women and children.
articles.nri_angle: The venous-blood survey resets the anaemia numbers diaspora families cite when elderly parents and children in India are tested, and targets treatment at moderate and severe cases.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Runs More Military Exercises With US Than Any Other Country
articles.excerpt: A US fact sheet on the Major Defense Partnership catalogues a 2026 calendar spanning Yudh Abhyas, Tarang Shakti, Tiger Triumph and Malabar, alongside the Javelin deal and a first Quad joint exercise planned for 2027.
articles.image_caption: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor (centre) poses with Indian Navy officers, including Rear Admiral Srinivas Maddula, and US personnel aboard the aircraft carrier USS George Washington on November 20, 2026. Gor used the visit to highlight expanding India-US military cooperation, joint exercises and information sharing.
articles.nri_angle: The exercise record underpins the US-India strategic relationship that shapes everything from Indo-Pacific security to defence jobs in both countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Food Regulator to Take Bisleri to Court Over Unsafe Water Sample
articles.excerpt: The FSSAI sanctioned prosecution after one lab found a Bisleri packaged-water sample over bromate limits and a referral lab, on the company's own appeal, detected PAHs and also declared it unsafe.
articles.nri_angle: Bisleri is the bottled-water brand most India travellers and returning NRIs reach for first; a prosecution over an unsafe sample is a consumer-safety story for every visit home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi and Nepal's Balen Shah to Flag Off Ayodhya–Janakpur Express on November 23
articles.excerpt: The weekly direct service links Ayodhya Dham and Janakpur Dham over about 604 km with 10 intermediate stops; inaugural specials run November 23–25, with fares and the full regular timetable still to be published.
articles.image_caption: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah (left) and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The two leaders are scheduled to jointly flag off the Ayodhya-Janakpur Express on November 23.
articles.nri_angle: A direct Ayodhya–Janakpur train gives diaspora pilgrims a single-train Ramayana-circuit journey between India and Nepal for the first time.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

rows: Weekly — Saturdays from Janakpur Dham, Mondays from Ayodhya Cantt
data_cards.title: Ayodhya–Janakpur Express at a glance

articles.title: Manipur Spurious Liquor Death Toll Rises to 17, About 230 People in Hospital
articles.excerpt: Sixteen of the dead are from Chandel district and one from Kakching. Officials say 1,130 people have been screened, six arrests made and 4,600 litres of illicit liquor seized.
articles.nri_angle: For Manipuri families abroad, the confirmed figures — 17 dead, about 230 admitted, screening locations and hospital names — are the verified update to share instead of circulating rumours.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Dedicates Nitish Setu, New Six-Lane Ganga Bridge in Bihar
articles.excerpt: The 19.7 km Kachhi Dargah–Bidupur crossing links Patna and Vaishali districts and anchors a ₹34,470 crore package of Bihar projects inaugurated on Saturday.
articles.nri_angle: A new Ganga crossing cutting Patna–Vaishali travel to about 20-25 minutes matters to diaspora families traveling to north Bihar.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Air India Crash Probe in Final Stage, Government Tells Supreme Court
articles.excerpt: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta sought two to three weeks to finish the AI171 investigation as the court weighs petitions for an independent probe.
articles.image_caption: The tail section of Air India flight AI171 in the wreckage of the Ahmedabad building the aircraft struck after take-off in June 2025.
articles.nri_angle: AI171 was an Ahmedabad-London flight carrying many diaspora families; its final report is the document relatives in India, the UK and North America have waited 17 months for.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi at IIT Kharagpur's 75th Year: 'Break the Limits, Unlock the Possibilities'
articles.excerpt: At the platinum jubilee of India's first IIT, the Prime Minister interacted with 75 students, unveiled a commemorative coin, and pointed to poverty numbers, chip exports and Skyroot's rocket as proof that 'too late' is a mindset.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addresses the platinum jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur.
articles.nri_angle: IIT Kharagpur's alumni are spread across the diaspora's tech and space industries — Modi's shout-out to Skyroot co-founder Pawan Kumar Chandana, an alumnus, lands directly with them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Court Dispatches Summonses to Doval, Goel in Pannun Case via Delhi Courts
articles.excerpt: The Southern District of New York sent the summonses by FedEx to the Patiala House, Tis Hazari and Dwarka courts under the Hague Convention, after service through India's central authority was attempted and rejected — a route New Delhi says is not lawful.
articles.image_caption: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval, photographed at an event.
articles.nri_angle: The service fight decides whether a US civil suit naming India's NSA and a former R&AW chief can proceed at all — a case diaspora readers have followed since the 2023 murder-for-hire allegations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Pannun filed the civil suit in the Southern District of New York.
India rejected the suit as 'fabricated and malicious'.
US court authorized service through Indian courts.

articles.title: India Crosses 1 Crore HPV Vaccine Doses in Less Than Nine Months
articles.excerpt: The national campaign has reached nearly 87% of its target cohort of 14-year-old girls, with six states reporting full coverage of their identified populations.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families with relatives in India, the free single-dose programme means a 14-year-old daughter or niece can be vaccinated at a government facility with a slot booked on U-WIN.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi to Unveil Rs 34,470 Crore of Bihar Projects on Three-State Saturday Tour
articles.excerpt: The Prime Minister's Saturday runs from IIT Kharagpur's 75th anniversary to a Rs 34,470 crore Bihar programme centred on the Nitish Setu Ganga bridge, and ends at the national skills ceremony in Lucknow.
articles.nri_angle: Sets out what Saturday's three-state programme means in practical terms for families in Bihar — a new Ganga bridge, power capacity, electric buses and PMAY-Urban house entries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's First Bullet Train to Run in Last Quarter of 2027, Surat-Vapi First
articles.excerpt: Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw says the first high-speed service will open between Surat and Vapi, with the full Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor following in phases and track trials of the indigenous B28 trainset expected by mid-2027.
articles.image_caption: An E5 Series Shinkansen, the train type planned for India's Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor (file photo)
articles.nri_angle: Gives diaspora travellers planning India trips a firm, sourced timeline: the first high-speed section opens in late 2027 between Surat and Vapi, not yet as a Mumbai-Ahmedabad through service.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

rows: Track trials of the B28 trainset
data_cards.title: How the Corridor Opens

articles.title: 11 Dead, 181 Hospitalised After Suspected Spurious Liquor in Manipur's Chandel District
articles.excerpt: Deaths over three days in Chakpikarong subdivision are linked to liquor reportedly bought in Sugnu; doctors suspect methanol poisoning as the chief minister orders an enquiry and hospitals in Imphal treat 181 patients.
articles.image_caption: A patient who fell ill after allegedly consuming spurious liquor is treated at a hospital in Imphal as officials and medical staff visit the ward.
articles.nri_angle: A public-health tragedy in Manipur with a clear safety advisory for anyone in the region; covered for diaspora readers with family in the Northeast.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan Begins Landfall Near Gopalpur; Over 3 Lakh Evacuated in Odisha
articles.excerpt: The storm crossed the coast near Gopalpur at 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph on Friday morning after weakening from a severe cyclonic storm, with 423 rescue teams deployed, dozens of trains cancelled and a red alert in two north Andhra districts.
articles.image_caption: Satellite image of Cyclone Akvan over the Bay of Bengal on November 18, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora readers with family along the Odisha and north Andhra coast get the landfall timing, evacuation scale, train cancellations and closure dates in one place.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Heat-Linked Gene Variant Helps Male Malaria Mosquitoes Mate, May Aid Transmission
articles.excerpt: A Cell study of Anopheles stephensi, the urban malaria vector native to South Asia, finds a deletion in the timeless clock gene gives males a mating edge in high heat while leaving females easier for the malaria parasite to infect.
articles.image_caption: Blood-feeding female Anopheles stephensi mosquitoes. The species, native to South Asia, is the subject of a Cell study linking a timeless-gene variant to heat adaptation and malaria transmission.
articles.nri_angle: Anopheles stephensi is the urban malaria mosquito native to India and South Asia, so a heat adaptation that could raise transmission matters for Indian cities and for diaspora families who travel into its range.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: Over 80,000 Evacuated in Odisha as Landfall Nears Friday Noon
articles.excerpt: Evacuations have risen past 80,000 against a 2-lakh target, 74 rescue teams are deployed, and the IMD now fixes Akvan's landfall between Narsapur and Puri, close to east of Gopalpur, by noon on Friday, November 20.
articles.image_caption: Waves pound a shoreline under grey skies as people watch from the beach, with Cyclone Akvan approaching the Odisha-Andhra coast. Odisha has evacuated more than 80,000 people ahead of the expected landfall on Friday, November 20.
articles.nri_angle: Readers with family in coastal Odisha and north Andhra Pradesh face a Friday-noon landfall, with trains and a Chennai–Yangon flight already cancelled or rescheduled.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Signs ₹1,976 Crore Deal With Israel's IAI to Upgrade Navy's Barak Missiles
articles.excerpt: The contract upgrades seven Barak-1 point defence systems — launchers, radars and command systems bought in 2000 — with new hardware and software, with BEL and BDL as IAI's industry partners in India.
articles.image_caption: Officials pose with the signed contract documents in New Delhi after the Ministry of Defence signed the Barak upgrade contract with Israel Aerospace Industries. The ₹1,976.40 crore deal covers hardware and software upgrades to seven Barak-1 point defence systems on Indian Navy warships.
articles.nri_angle: The upgrade keeps a 25-year-old Israeli-supplied shield on India's frontline warships while the indigenous VL-SRSAM replacement is developed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Two contracts signed for Barak-1 systems and missiles
Defence Acquisition Council approved the upgrade

articles.title: Tanker With Three Indians Hit Near Hormuz; Accounts Differ on Crew Casualties
articles.excerpt: India's shipping minister says all three Indian seafarers and the whole crew of the MT Navig8 Messi are safe; the operator reports one crew member missing and 11 injured.
articles.nri_angle: Indian seafarers crew a large share of the world's merchant fleet; three Indians were aboard the Navig8 Messi, and one Indian from the Tara Gas attack two days earlier is still missing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: MT Tara Gas attacked, one Indian seafarer missing.
MT Navig8 Messi attacked, conflicting reports emerge.
India's minister confirms all crew safe.

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan Veers North and Weakens; Landfall Window Now Narsapur to Puri
articles.excerpt: The IMD's revised forecast moves the November 20 landfall zone into Odisha's reach, cuts the expected intensity to a severe cyclonic storm, and puts 10 Andhra Pradesh districts on rain alert.
articles.image_caption: A satellite image shows Cyclone Akvan over the Bay of Bengal, east of India's coast.
articles.nri_angle: Families in the US and Gulf with relatives in coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha should note the landfall point is still uncertain; IMD updates on Wednesday night are the next reliable marker.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bombay High Court Quashes ICICI Bank's Sanction to Prosecute Chanda Kochhar
articles.excerpt: Justice Milind Jadhav held that the RBI, not ICICI Bank's board, is the competent authority to sanction prosecution of a bank's head under the Prevention of Corruption Act, and that the bank failed to apply its mind.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay High Court building in Mumbai, seen from across the Oval Maidan.
articles.nri_angle: The ruling is a closely watched governance test for India's largest private-sector banks, whose shares are widely held by NRI and foreign institutional investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Naidu Seeks Immediate Central Aid as Two Cyclones Leave Losses Above ₹7,000 Crore
articles.excerpt: The Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister briefed Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in Delhi on Tuesday, with preliminary estimates putting combined damage from Cyclones Arnav and Murasu above ₹7,000 crore.
articles.image_caption: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu review documents at their meeting in New Delhi. Naidu sought immediate Central assistance after Cyclones Arnav and Murasu caused losses the state preliminarily estimates at more than Rs 7,000 crore.
articles.nri_angle: Andhra Pradesh families in the diaspora are watching both the relief decision and a third approaching cyclone, Akvan, due to make landfall on November 20.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Central assessment team completes field inspections in four Andhra districts; state puts Murasu damage at ₹2,484.43 crore
Naidu meets Finance Minister Sitharaman in New Delhi and seeks immediate Central assistance
Cyclone Akvan forecast to make landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast

articles.title: US Loses Measles Elimination Status After 26 Years as Cases Pass 5,400
articles.excerpt: PAHO ruled on November 17 that measles has circulated uninterrupted in the United States for more than a year. Mexico and Bolivia lost their status in the same announcement.
articles.image_caption: A Pennsylvania Department of Health flyer advertises a measles vaccination clinic held on November 4, 2026. Pennsylvania has reported the most measles cases of any state this year, as the United States lost its measles elimination status.
articles.nri_angle: With measles endemic again in the US, Indian families there — and relatives visiting from India — should check MMR records, especially for infants and school-age children.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Music Economy Generated Rs 17,401 Crore in Gross Value in 2025, EY Finds
articles.excerpt: The EY-IPRS report puts economy-wide music value up 45% since 2023, with independent music at 43% of digital consumption — while direct recording and publishing revenue was Rs 5,433 crore and only 55% of surveyed authors earn full-time from music.
articles.nri_angle: Indian music's growth is increasingly driven by independent regional artists and streaming, the same catalogue diaspora listeners consume abroad; 19% of streams of Indian music on the platforms IPRS tracked were generated outside India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.title: Where the Rs 17,401 Crore Came From (2025)

articles.title: Two Killed, Including a Three-Year-Old, as Delhi House Collapses in Jwala Nagar
articles.excerpt: Six tenants were pulled from the Vivek Vihar building in Shahdara and taken to Hedgewar Hospital; officials say the first-floor slab and girder gave way, and the cause is still under investigation.
articles.nri_angle: Building collapses in ageing, densely rented housing are a recurring safety concern in Delhi that diaspora families with relatives in such homes follow closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: At Least 8 Killed as Bus Plunges Into 100-Metre Gorge in Tehri Garhwal
articles.excerpt: The Haridwar-Chamoli bus lost control near Gular Bazar at about 4:30 a.m. on Tuesday and fell below the bridge on the Rishikesh-Badrinath highway; 26 injured passengers were pulled out as the rescue continued.
articles.image_caption: The wrecked bus lies in a stream at the bottom of the gorge near Gular Bazar in Tehri Garhwal, with police and rescue personnel at the scene. The Haridwar to Chamoli bus fell nearly 100 metres from the Rishikesh-Badrinath highway early on Tuesday, killing at least eight people.
articles.nri_angle: The crash was on the Rishikesh-Badrinath highway, the Char Dham pilgrim route also used by NRI families visiting Uttarakhand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
